- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for downward surprise.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > history peak), model frequently overcorrects downward; apply a “lag correction” — keep forecast 1–2 days above true trend.
- If sentiment flips from positive to negative mid-period, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope sharply in next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window; apply a “first 7 days discount” — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day for first 7 days.
